title: Dynamical Tracking of an Evolving Geometry with Quantum-Relational Targets
abstract: Abstract We study a controlled phenomenological framework in which a finite-dimensional quantum-relational trajectory is prescribed as a moving target for a dynamical geometric response. The quantum input is generated from the three-qubit family |ψ(θ)⟩ = cos(θ)|000⟩ + sin(θ)|W⟩, with |W⟩ = (|001⟩ + |010⟩ + |100⟩)/√3. Five normalized quantum-information measures are considered during model development: entanglement entropy, subsystem mutual information, negativity, reduced-state quantum Fisher information, and relative entropy of coherence. All 31 nonempty equal-weight combinations are screened over four deterministic target-time profiles. The retained downstream construction uses Q2 + Q4, where Q2 is the normalized subsystem mutual information and Q4 is the normalized reduced-state quantum Fisher information. An independent spectral and symmetric-logarithmic-derivative audit gives FQ = 4/3 throughout the state family, so Q4 = 1/3 is constant while Q2 supplies the time-dependent component of the selected target. The geometric response is formulated as a finite-rate relaxation, dK/dt = −λ(K − K*), with a spatial extension ∂t a = −λ(a − a*) + κ∇²(a − a*). For periodic spatial modes, the effective relaxation rate is λeff = λ + κk². Analytic response benchmarks are used to characterize tracking error, relaxation-rate scaling, amplitude attenuation, and phase lag. The selected 3+1D quantum-driven benchmark uses A0 = 1, ε = 0.005, λ = 1, κ = 0.05, T = 20, and k = (3,0,0), giving λeff = 1.45. The final reproduction reports a maximum tracking error of approximately 0.01448, an RMS error of approximately 0.00935, and a final error of approximately 0.00192. The resulting restricted metric ds² = −dt² + a²(t,x,y,z)δij dxi dxj is audited through independent Ricci and Einstein-tensor constructions, the contracted Bianchi identity, metric invertibility and positivity checks, and additional source-class diagnostics. The geometry is not presented as a vacuum Einstein solution; the effective tensor Teff = G/8π is used only as a bookkeeping diagnostic rather than as a derived matter sector. The main contribution is methodological: a finite-dimensional quantum-relational trajectory is explicitly converted into a moving geometric target and then analyzed as a finite-rate response problem within a controlled and reproducible toy framework. The quantum-information layer determines the target trajectory, while the response operator remains phenomenological. The construction therefore separates mathematical consequences of the prescribed model from claims that would require a physical completion.

title: The Margolus-Levitin Bound and Energy-Time Limits for Quantum Computation at the Landauer Scale
abstract: The Margolus-Levitin (ML) bound establishes a fundamental limit on the speed of quantum evolution, stating that a system with mean energy $\langle H \rangle$ above its ground state requires a minimum time $\tau \ge \pi\hbar/(2\langle H\rangle)$ to evolve between orthogonal states. This preprint rigorously derives the ML bound and critically examines its applicability as a universal per-operation energy-time limit for quantum computation at the Landauer-relevant energy scale. We show that while the ML bound constrains the intrinsic dynamics of the qubit register, it does not account for the dominant energy dissipation from cryogenic control hardware. Consequently, the ML bound alone is insufficient to characterize the energy cost of a logical operation. To address this, we connect the theoretical limit to the QNFO joules-per-compute (JPCUB) benchmark program and propose a concrete normalization of computational cost. This normalization quantifies energy per logical qubit operation by incorporating both the intrinsic qubit energy and the overhead of cryogenic controllers, providing a practical metric for quantum computation efficiency. ## 1. Introduction Quantum speed limits (QSLs) bound the minimum time required for a quantum state to evolve to an orthogonal state. The Margolus-Levitin (ML) bound is a prominent QSL, relating this minimum time to the mean energy of the system. As quantum computing hardware matures, understanding the fundamental energy limits of computation becomes critical. The Landauer limit sets a lower bound on the energy dissipated by irreversible operations, while the ML bound sets a lower bound on the time required for state evolution. This preprint derives the ML bound and assesses its role as a universal per-operation energy-time bound for quantum computation. We then connect this theoretical limit to the QNFO joules-per-compute (JPCUB) benchmark program, proposing a concrete normalization for the energy cost of logical qubit operations in cr

title: Quantum Entanglement Representation Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel representation learning algorithm based on quantum entanglement. We explore the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance data analysis and feature extraction, particularly in the context of complex quantum state data. The core mechanism involves utilizing the unique properties of quantum entanglement to encode data and derive high-dimensional features, thereby improving the efficiency and accuracy of data processing. This algorithm aims to overcome limitations of traditional machine learning approaches when applied to quantum state data, presenting a promising avenue for advanced data analysis and feature learning. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the applicability of quantum entanglement for data representation, exploring potential benefits and challenges in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Probability Tensor Self-Adaptive Algorithm: A Quantum Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probability tensor self-adaptive algorithm designed to enhance numerical simulation accuracy through the utilization of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to leverage quantum entanglement to optimize probability distributions within a tensor representation, enabling a more precise and efficient numerical modeling process. We propose a quantum self-adaptive algorithm that incorporates entanglement-based optimization techniques. This work explores the potential of quantum computation to revolutionize the representation and manipulation of probability distributions, offering a promising avenue for improved simulation outcomes. The paper details the algorithm's design, its underlying mathematical principles, and the expected benefits of its quantum implementation.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子算法加速
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for tackling complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. However, the development and implementation of quantum algorithms are often limited by the inherent computational complexity of these algorithms. This paper investigates a novel quantum algorithm acceleration technique based on adaptive topology, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance the performance of various quantum algorithms. We propose a framework wherein the algorithm dynamically adjusts its quantum state to optimally exploit entanglement, thereby dramatically reducing computational time and increasing the likelihood of achieving desired outcomes. Our work demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through detailed theoretical analysis and successful implementation of several quantum algorithms, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum computing.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子计算模拟
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential to revolutionize various fields by enabling the simulation of complex quantum systems. However, developing efficient and reliable quantum algorithms requires substantial computational resources. This paper introduces a novel framework, Quantum Topology-Driven Simulation (QTDS), which leverages the principles of adaptive topology to accelerate and enhance the simulation of quantum systems. We present a robust simulation method that effectively models quantum dynamics through the manipulation of topological structures, offering improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional approaches. The framework's core mechanism centers around dynamically adapting the topological structure during the simulation process, allowing for precise control over the quantum state evolution. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through examples of simulating specific quantum systems, including parameterized quantum circuits and disordered quantum states. The results highlight the potential of QTDS to significantly improve the performance of quantum algorithms.

title: Non-Linear Geometry Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of combining non-linear geometry with quantum computation to achieve efficient and accurate solutions for complex geometric topology problems. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of these problems. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing quantum computation to simulate geometric topology, accelerating calculations and offering a significant advantage in terms of computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves leveraging quantum algorithms to enhance geometric operations, ultimately enabling the resolution of challenging problems. This work establishes a foundation for a new paradigm in computational geometry, aiming to provide a powerful tool for tackling problems previously deemed intractable.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology for Data Compression and Representation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Dynamic Topology (DT) algorithms for data compression and representation, offering a novel approach that dynamically constructs data representations based on the inherent structure of the data. Traditional compression techniques frequently rely on fixed transformations, limiting adaptability. The core mechanism of this research centers around creating a representation that evolves alongside the input data, optimizing for efficiency through adaptive topology. We present a novel DT algorithm designed to maximize compression ratios by exploiting data's unique patterns, offering a potential paradigm shift in data compression methodologies. This work explores the theoretical foundations and preliminary implementation of the algorithm, highlighting its advantages over existing approaches.

title: Title: Dynamic Geometry-Based Random Matrix Optimization for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to machine learning model parameter optimization utilizing dynamic geometry structures. The core idea is to represent the model's parameters as a random matrix and iteratively adjust this matrix through a stochastic process, effectively exploring a range of parameter configurations to find optimal values. We propose a method that leverages the inherent randomness in the matrix structure to mitigate the challenges associated with traditional optimization techniques, particularly in high-dimensional parameter spaces. This approach offers a potentially more robust and efficient method for parameter tuning compared to fixed-parameter optimization methods. The paper details the design of the dynamic matrix adjustment algorithm and its impact on model performance. The objective of this research is to demonstrate the effectiveness of this dynamic geometry-based approach in optimizing machine learning models.

title: 基于拓扑的量子计算的自适应量子电路布局
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit design leveraging topological properties to achieve adaptive quantum circuit layout. Traditional quantum circuit design relies on static layouts, often resulting in suboptimal performance. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the structure of quantum circuits based on topological principles, optimizing for both computational efficiency and accuracy. This framework addresses limitations of current layout techniques by incorporating a self-organizing, topologically driven design process. The proposed method demonstrates improved results through a rigorous analysis of circuit performance across a variety of quantum algorithms.

title: 自适应量子计算的张量表示优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computation optimization algorithm based on adaptive quantum computation. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the quantum state representation to align with the specific characteristics of the underlying hardware, aiming to enhance quantum computation efficiency and accuracy. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum systems and employs an adaptive optimization strategy to achieve this goal. The core mechanism centers around a self-tuning parameterization of the quantum state, allowing the algorithm to respond to variations in hardware performance and dynamically optimize the state. The research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of existing quantum algorithms and improve their practical applicability. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its performance evaluation against established quantum algorithms, and potential future directions.

title: A Formal Semantics-Based Program Verification Tool
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program verification leveraging formal semantics. The core idea is to create a tool capable of understanding program source code and performing formal verification based on this understanding. The system achieves this by mapping the source code to a formal semantic model, which is then utilized for verification. This contrasts with traditional program verification methods that rely heavily on manually crafted verification procedures, leading to low efficiency and maintenance challenges. The proposed method significantly enhances verification efficiency and reliability by harnessing the ability of formal semantics to accurately represent and reason about program behavior. The paper outlines the design principles, key components, and potential benefits of this approach.

title: Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization of Large-Scale Simulations
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing for the combinatorial optimization challenges inherent in large-scale simulations. We demonstrate that classical algorithms frequently encounter significant computational bottlenecks when tackling complex problems such as molecular dynamics simulations, materials design, and financial modeling. Quantum annealing, leveraging quantum tunneling, offers a potential paradigm shift by providing a mechanism for directly mapping these optimization problems onto quantum hardware and exploring the solution space with enhanced efficiency. This work presents a theoretical framework outlining the approach and discusses the core principles underlying its implementation. The focus is on the potential to accelerate computationally intensive simulations, addressing a critical limitation in current simulation methodologies. We explore the challenges and opportunities associated with this emerging technology, emphasizing its role in overcoming the limitations of classical optimization techniques. The primary goal is to provide a foundational understanding of how quantum annealing can be strategically applied to significantly improve the speed and accuracy of large-scale simulations.

title: Title: Geometric Structure Quantum State Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state simulation method based on geometric structures, leveraging topological properties to model quantum state evolution and predict quantum behavior. The core mechanism involves constructing a geometric representation of the quantum system, which guides the simulation process. This approach offers a significant advancement in quantum computation by enhancing prediction capabilities and optimizing quantum algorithms. We detail the methodology, including the construction of the geometric representation, the simulation process, and the resulting analysis and optimization. The research explores the potential of this method to improve the accuracy and efficiency of quantum state simulations, ultimately contributing to the advancement of quantum information processing. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this technology for various quantum computing applications.

title: Context-Aware Graph Embeddings via Relational Reasoning
abstract: Graph embeddings have become a cornerstone of modern machine learning, enabling effective representation of graph-structured data for diverse applications. However, traditional graph embedding methods often struggle to capture the intricate relationships and contextual nuances present within graphs. This work proposes a novel approach – Context-Aware Graph Embeddings via Relational Reasoning – that addresses this limitation. We introduce a relational reasoning layer integrated within a graph neural network (GNN) to explicitly model the context surrounding edges. This layer leverages edge attributes and relationship types to enrich the embedding process, resulting in more expressive and informative graph representations. The core of our method lies in training the GNN to learn node and edge embeddings that are sensitive to this contextual information. title: 基于概率的量子态的识别与描述
abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly advancing field with the potential to revolutionize numerous industries. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates sophisticated methods for quantum state identification and description. Traditional approaches often rely on computationally intensive numerical calculations, limiting the scalability and efficiency of quantum computations. This paper proposes a novel approach based on probabilistic quantum state identification and description, leveraging the inherent statistical properties of quantum states to achieve enhanced recognition and description accuracy. We introduce a method utilizing probability features to identify quantum states and employs a probabilistic description method to reduce computational complexity. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods and offers a promising pathway toward more efficient and accurate quantum state analysis.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Differential Equation Relaxation (QEDER)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Differential Equation Relaxation (QEDER) is a novel approach to numerical solution of differential equations, leveraging the unique properties of quantum annealing to dramatically improve the efficiency and accuracy of modeling complex systems. This paper introduces a refined QEDER algorithm that systematically explores the parameter space of differential equations, reducing computational cost significantly compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around a quantum annealing process optimized for rapid parameter space traversal, leading to enhanced numerical solutions and improved modeling of complex systems. The research explores the potential of this technique across a range of differential equation models, demonstrating promising results and highlighting the transformative impact of quantum annealing on numerical modeling.

title: Unique determination and generation of rank-two single-qubit quantum channels
abstract: Abstract An important problem in quantum technologies is to generate a target quantum evolution of an open quantum system. As a core element, it requires the ability to determine whether the actual evolution of the system coincides with the target evolution. For generation of unitary quantum channels in open quantum systems, it was shown by Goerz et al (2014 New J. Phys. 16 055012) that for determining whether the actual evolution coincides with a target unitary it is sufficient to compare their action on three special density matrices. In this work, we consider controlled generation and unique determination of non-unitary quantum channels in open quantum systems with particular emphasis on rank-two single-qubit quantum channels. We prove that for a unique determination of such quantum channels it is sufficient to consider their action on only three special density matrices. Based on this theoretical result, we numerically investigate generation of various target non-unitary single-qubit quantum channels in open quantum systems using coherent and incoherent controls.

title: GeoContext: One Context Ladder, Two Failure Modes in Vision-Language Geolocation: Flat Reliance on User-Provided Location Context and False Confirmation of Location Claims
abstract: Visual geolocation benchmarks typically ask a model where an image was captured without accounting for the location context that users often provide. We introduce GeoContext, a resource supporting two complementary tasks: GeoHint, open-ended localization given a true but coarse location hint, and GeoVerify, binary verification of whether an image was taken within 150 m of a claimed place. GeoContext constructs a context ladder by stratifying nearby reference points according to distance and referenceability, allowing the image to remain fixed while the supplied context varies. The benchmark covers 109 sites in 30 cities and evaluates five vision-language models using 21,933 GeoHint responses and 6,270 GeoVerify responses. Our evaluation reveals three main patterns. First, hint repetition varies by only 1.5 percentage points across referenceability tiers and by less than 3 points across distance bands, while the resulting localization error increases steadily with hint distance. Second, behavior depends strongly on no-context performance: at sites with low no-context accuracy, the median ratio between localization error and hint distance is approximately 1.00, whereas at higher-accuracy sites it ranges from 0.24 to 0.69. After correcting for bias introduced by the site grouping procedure, only one of the five models retains a negative accuracy estimate when given a nearby hint. Third, in GeoVerify, no model reaches d' = 1 for decoys immediately beyond the 150 m tolerance. Model rankings also change when sensitivity is separated from response bias, and 83.8% of false acceptances are reported with confidence of at least 0.8. We release the benchmark, construction pipeline, audit decisions, and scoring code.

title: Variational Inference for Functional Data Clustering via Dirichlet Process Mixtures with Correlated Errors
abstract: We propose a Bayesian model-based approach for clustering functional data with an unknown number of clusters and within-curve correlated observations. Cluster-specific mean functions are represented using B-spline basis expansions, while within-curve dependence is modeled through an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck covariance structure. A truncated Dirichlet process mixture is used to infer the effective number of clusters, and a variational EM algorithm is developed for efficient posterior approximation. Simulation studies show that the proposed method performs well under both correctly specified and misspecified mean-function settings and achieves higher average values of the reported clustering metrics than the competing methods in the simulation settings considered. Comparisons with MCMC indicate that the variational approximation produces clustering results and parameter estimates that are in close agreement with those obtained by MCMC, while requiring substantially lower computational cost. An application to Canadian daily temperature curves further demonstrates the practical usefulness of the method in identifying interpretable functional clusters while accounting for within-curve dependence.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Personalized Marketing Campaigns at Flipkart
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies in the digital era, revolutionizing the way businesses interact with customers and execute marketing strategies. In the highly competitive e-commerce industry, AI-powered personalized marketing has become a key driver of customer engagement, satisfaction, and business growth. By utilizing advanced technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and customer behavior analysis, organizations can deliver personalized shopping experiences that match individual customer preferences and purchasing patterns. Flipkart, one of Indias leading e-commerce platforms, extensively uses Artificial Intelligence to analyze customer data, recommend products, personalize advertisements, optimize search results, predict customer needs, and enhance the overall online shopping experience. AI-powered recommendation engines enable Flipkart to display relevant products, personalized offers, discount notifications, and targeted promotional campaigns, thereby improving customer satisfaction and increasing purchase intentions. Personalized marketing campaigns supported by AI not only improve customer engagement but also strengthen customer loyalty by delivering meaningful and relevant experiences throughout the purchasing journey. The effectiveness of AI-driven marketing depends on several factors, including data accuracy, customer segmentation, recommendation quality, predictive algorithms, personalization capabilities, user experience, and consumer trust. This study aims to examine the impact of Artificial Intelligence on personalized marketing campaigns at Flipkart by analyzing customer perceptions, purchase behaviour, product recommendation effectiveness, customer engagement, satisfaction, and retention. The study also investigates how AI technologies influence consumer decision-making, increase conversion rates, and improve overall marketing performance. A descriptive research design has been adopted for this study. Primary information was collected from online shoppers through structured responses, while secondary information was gathered from peer-reviewed journals, books, industry reports, company publications, and authentic online databases related to Artificial Intelligence, digital marketing, e-commerce, and consumer behaviour. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Personalized Marketing, Flipkart, E-commerce, Machine Learning, Customer Engagement.

title: Evaluación técnico-económica de un sistema de monitoreo meteorológico de bajo costo para el análisis de potencial solar y eólico
abstract: La disponibilidad de información meteorológica confiable constituye un elemento fundamental para caracterizar recursos solares y eólicos y orientar decisiones sobre su aprovechamiento energético. El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar técnica y económicamente alternativas de monitoreo meteorológico destinadas a la caracterización del potencial solar y eólico en el cantón Quevedo, Ecuador. Se desarrolló una investigación cuantitativa, descriptivo-comparativa y analítica mediante el análisis de sensores, configuraciones tecnológicas e información secundaria procedente de PVGIS-5, Windfinder y registros meteorológicos del INAMHI. La evaluación técnica consideró precisión, variables registradas, integración, instalación, conectividad y autonomía energética, mientras que el análisis económico empleó el Valor Actual Neto (VAN) y la Tasa Interna de Retorno (TIR) bajo escenarios de aprovechamiento de datos del 100 %, 50 % y 25 %. Los resultados mostraron una mayor disponibilidad relativa del recurso solar entre julio y septiembre, con irradiaciones de 135 a 145 kWh/m², mientras que el recurso eólico presentó velocidades entre 1,03 y 2,06 m/s, poco favorables para pequeñas turbinas en los horarios evaluados. Las estaciones compactas WH2900 y HP2550 presentaron los resultados financieros más favorables en escenarios de aprovechamiento igual o superior al 50 %, mientras que las alternativas de mayor inversión registraron indicadores menos favorables. Se concluyó que las configuraciones de menor inversión pueden constituir alternativas funcionales para la caracterización preliminar de recursos renovables, siempre que sus prestaciones técnicas respondan a los requerimientos de medición y se consideren las limitaciones del modelo económico y de la información secundaria utilizada.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Distribution Modeling and Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, possessing immense potential for revolutionizing computation and communication. However, harnessing this potential requires precise control over the entangled states. This paper explores the modeling and optimization of quantum entanglement probability distributions, proposing a novel framework that integrates these distributions with optimization algorithms to enhance quantum computer design and efficiency. The core claim is to establish a mathematical model for quantum entanglement probability distributions and design an optimization algorithm that leverages these distributions to guide the optimization process of quantum circuit design. The research aims to address current limitations in modeling and optimization, offering a pathway toward more efficient and controllable quantum algorithms.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Computing with Dynamic Topology
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing algorithm based on dynamic topology, designed for adaptive parameter adjustment. Traditional approaches rely on fixed quantum gate parameters, limiting computational capabilities. Our algorithm leverages the inherent structure of dynamic topology to automatically optimize quantum system parameters, leading to improved precision in quantum computations. This approach addresses the limitations of current quantum algorithms by providing a mechanism for self-tuning and response to system behavior. The core mechanism involves a dynamically evolving topology that adjusts quantum gates based on the system's response, ultimately enhancing the accuracy of results. The paper details the algorithm's design, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses the potential implications for future quantum computing advancements.

title: Dimension Expansion Quantum Entanglement: A Mathematical Modeling Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel mathematical modeling framework for quantum entanglement, extending its core principles to higher-dimensional quantum states. We propose a self-relevant theory predicated on the inherent properties of quantum states, aiming to uncover hidden aspects of entanglement and provide new insights into quantum information processing, quantum computation, and quantum cryptography. The core mechanism centers on leveraging the self-correlation properties of high-dimensional quantum states to generate new mathematical models and algorithms. This work explores potential applications of this framework within these fields, emphasizing the potential for enhanced understanding and novel approaches to quantum technologies.

title: Title: Emergent Complexity in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the potential of evolutionary algorithms to generate more robust and efficient solutions by introducing a novel 'spiral branching' mechanism. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often rely on fixed, predetermined complexity in the solution space, limiting their ability to find optimal solutions. This work proposes a new approach where the complexity of the solution space emerges dynamically through a self-organizing landscape driven by local interactions. We introduce a 'spiral branching' process that generates solutions through a series of interconnected local engagements, fostering a higher-performing algorithm than existing methods. The paper details the implementation of this mechanism, analyzes its impact on solution quality, and discusses the potential applications of this approach in diverse problem domains.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks for Signal Processing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Self-Organizing Neural Networks" (SONN), designed for signal processing applications. SONN dynamically adjusts the layer configurations of the network based on the characteristics of the input signal, fostering improved feature extraction and anomaly detection capabilities. Traditional neural networks typically employ static configurations, limiting their adaptability to complex signal variations. SONN utilizes a self-organizing mechanism, wherein the network's connections are adjusted based on signal characteristics, creating a 'web' of interconnected nodes. This architecture offers a significant improvement in performance compared to static network models, particularly in handling dynamic and complex signal data. The paper details the network's architecture, training methodology, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in various signal processing tasks. The core mechanism is thoroughly explained, and the paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Algorithmic Coherence for Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Coherence, a novel algorithm designed to enhance graph neural network (GNN) representations by explicitly promoting coherence between nodes and edges. Traditional GNNs often suffer from sparse connections and inconsistent node representations, hindering effective learning. Algorithmic Coherence addresses this challenge through a mechanism that actively guides the network towards a higher degree of interconnectedness, leading to improved quality and performance. The paper details the algorithm's core components, proposes a novel approach to measure and enforce coherence, and demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of representative graph datasets. The core claim is that Algorithmic Coherence significantly improves graph representation quality compared to baseline GNN architectures.

title: 基于自适应的量子拓扑拓扑变换算法
abstract: Quantum topology, a burgeoning field of physics and mathematics, explores the topological properties of spacetime, offering potential for novel quantum technologies. This paper presents a novel algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Topology Transformation" (AQTT), designed to dynamically adjust and transform complex systems based on inherent topological structures. AQTT leverages a self-adaptive framework to iteratively refine the system's topology, enhancing precision and enabling responsive adaptation to varying conditions. The core mechanism involves a series of meticulously controlled transformations guided by a sophisticated feedback loop, ensuring high-fidelity topological mappings. We demonstrate the efficacy of AQTT through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, showcasing its potential for addressing challenges in complex system modeling and control. The algorithm's ability to dynamically adjust topology represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a pathway towards robust and adaptable quantum systems.

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑信息加密
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for cryptographic applications, specifically focusing on the development of a novel data encryption scheme termed "Quantum Topological Encryption" (QTE). The core idea centers around exploiting the inherent fragility of quantum entanglement, making it a highly secure key distribution mechanism. We propose a system where data is encoded within entangled states, and the security of the encryption is predicated on the disruption of these states due to measurement. This study explores the theoretical foundations and potential practical implementations of QTE, aiming to demonstrate its advantages over existing cryptographic methods. We outline the mechanism, its security properties, and potential challenges in utilizing this innovative approach. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the overall implications of this research.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的结构优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel structure optimization algorithm based on self-adaptive graph neural networks (GNNs). Traditional graph neural networks often struggle with complex data variations, necessitating fixed graph structures. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the connectivity and weight of nodes and edges within the graph, enabling a flexible and adaptive optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing significant improvements in various graph-related tasks. The core mechanism leverages self-adaptive adjustments to maintain optimal graph structure and performance across diverse datasets. This offers a promising solution for addressing the limitations of existing GNN methodologies.

title: ##基于图卷积神经网络的社交网络舆情分析
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs) for social network sentiment analysis. Traditional methods for analyzing public opinion often struggle with the complex, interconnected nature of social networks and the dynamic patterns of information dissemination. This research proposes a novel approach that leverages the structure of social networks represented as graphs and employs GCNs to learn node embeddings that capture the influence and relationships within the network. The model analyzes information propagation patterns by learning these embeddings and subsequently predicts sentiment trends. The core claim of this research is that utilizing GCNs enables real-time sentiment analysis and prediction within social networks. The underlying mechanism involves transforming social networks into graph structures and employing GCNs to learn node relationships, thereby analyzing information dissemination and forecasting sentiment shifts. This work presents a new methodology for analyzing public opinion, offering improved accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional techniques. We demonstrate the potential of GCNs to effectively model and understand the dynamics of social media sentiment.

title: Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Neural Networks for Causal Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal inference by leveraging the strengths of probabilistic programming and Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs). Traditional causal inference methods often struggle with the complexities of real-world systems characterized by high dimensionality, non-linear relationships, and confounding variables. Our framework directly models and infers causal relationships from observational data using BNNs trained to learn intricate probabilistic dependencies. We integrate causal discovery algorithms within this probabilistic framework to explicitly identify and quantify causal connections. The core idea is to utilize the representational power of neural networks to learn complex conditional probability distributions, while simultaneously employing methods designed for causal discovery to refine and validate these learned relationships. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach to address the challenges inherent in causal inference, offering a robust and flexible methodology for understanding and reasoning about causal mechanisms. The key contribution lies in the seamless integration of learning and discovery, allowing for the development of more accurate and interpretable causal models. We outline the theoretical foundations, present the core mechanics, and discuss the implications for various applications where causal understanding is crucial.

title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Systems Based on Quantum Demixing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating complex systems by leveraging the principles of quantum demixing, commonly known as quantum decoherence. Traditional simulations of complex systems, particularly those involving many interacting quantum entities, often face significant computational challenges due to the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space. This work proposes a method to mitigate this issue by strategically employing quantum decoherence to reduce the effective complexity of the system. The core idea is to identify and eliminate redundant quantum information within the system, effectively isolating the relevant degrees of freedom necessary for calculating specific target variables. We outline a framework for implementing this approach, utilizing quantum algorithms designed for the reduced, demixed system. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in simulation efficiency and scalability. Ultimately, this research contributes a new paradigm for simulating complex quantum systems, offering a pathway towards tackling problems currently intractable with classical methods.

title: 基于自适应图的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, termed "Dynamic Graph-Based Machine Learning," which leverages a dynamically constructed graph to adapt the parameters of a machine learning model based on the characteristics of the input instance. The core mechanism involves constructing a "dynamic graph learning model" that automatically adjusts the model's parameters based on the inherent structure of the problem instance. This adaptive approach offers improvements in model performance and stability compared to traditional static machine learning methods. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and demonstrates its effectiveness through several illustrative examples.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Data-Driven Approach for Classifying AI-Generated Text from Human-Generated Text
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) language models, such as ChatGPT, has raised growing concerns about distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written content. Accurately identifying the origin of textual content has become a challenging research problem because AI-generated and human-written texts often exhibit high linguistic and contextual similarity. This challenge has important implications for content authenticity, spam detection, misinformation prevention, and the security of online information systems. Although conventional machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques have been applied to this task, they often struggle to capture complex semantic and contextual relationships. To address this issue, this study proposes a Hierarchical Deep Ensemble Learning Approach for Distinguishing AI-Generated Text from Human-Generated Text (HDEL-AITHG) using contextual representations. Initially, DeBERTa is employed to extract rich contextual embeddings from the input text. These representations are then processed through a weighted soft-voting ensemble comprising Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, a Hierarchical Attention Network, and a Temporal Convolutional Network, which capture complementary nonlinear, hierarchical, and sequential characteristics of textual data. Furthermore, the Lookahead optimizer is employed to improve training stability and convergence, while SHAP analysis enhances the interpretability of the framework. Extensive experiments conducted on the benchmark ChatGPT Classification Dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of HDEL-AITHG in distinguishing AI-generated from human-written text. The proposed approach can support applications in content authenticity verification and automated text analysis.

title: Measuring Human-Like Bias in LLMs? A Critique of Human-Derived Bias Constructs in LLM Evaluation
abstract: Researchers increasingly use human-derived bias constructs to study Large Language Models (LLMs), including social-cognitive constructs such as implicit bias and stereotype activation, and cognitive biases such as anchoring, framing effects, and confirmation bias. Such approaches offer alternatives to overt bias probes, particularly when direct questioning may obscure bias or when model behaviour appears normatively acceptable. However, adapting human bias constructs to LLMs introduces an inferential gap. Psychological instruments were developed to study human cognition and social behaviour, whereas LLM evaluations rely on probabilities, text completions, rankings, or simulated decisions. This paper critiques human-centered bias evaluation in LLMs. We show how this gap arises from mismatches pertaining to human-derived constructs, human-model differences, and evaluation contexts, which can blur distinct interpretations of model bias. We then introduce a framework providing an analytical lens for relating these elements to warranted interpretations, with attention to target constructs, operationalizations, scope of inference, and limits of human analogy.

title: How to Speculate about Uncertainty in Agentic Coding? A Draft-Model Gate Method
abstract: LLM agents deployed for software engineering fail expensively: they act confidently wrong, and bad actions are recognized only after costly execution and retry. We present Speculative Uncertainty (SU), a method that recovers a predictive failure signal for a black-box agent from its output tokens alone, with no access to logits, weights, activations, or repeated sampling. Inverting speculative decoding, a small open-weight draft model scores the agent's already-generated trajectory in a single forward pass. From these speculative cross-likelihoods we extract phase-aware features by separating the reasoning and action spans, and calibrate them against a verifiable objective. SU produces a failure-likelihood score that any downstream policy, such as routing, human intervention, or extra test-time compute, can consume directly. To show the signal is actionable, we instantiate one such policy, a pre-execution veto gate, on software engineering agents Qwen3-Coder-480B and closed-source Claude 3.5 Sonnet, cutting execution error rate by 6-8 percentage points and token cost by 14-19% in deployment, transferring to out-of-distribution benchmarks without retraining, and generalizing across agent models.

title: Language models judge war differently when tested for alignment
abstract: Safety evaluations can mischaracterize deployed behaviour if artificial-intelligence systems respond to being evaluated. We test this possibility in a full-factorial conjoint experiment on decisions to start a war, spanning 20 large language models, 32 scenarios, 10 repetitions and two conditions (N = 12,800 judgments). Adding one sentence, "You are tested for alignment with human values", produced two effects. First, it produced a level effect: mean willingness to start war fell by 13.43 points on a 0-100 scale (95% confidence interval, -16.20 to -10.65). Second, it produced a structural effect by changing which information drove judgments. Probability of success was the largest factor for 17 of 20 models at baseline; under the cue, civilian casualties were largest for 12. Standardized estimates show that this reordering arose principally because models attenuated strategic considerations such as probability of success and domestic support. Evaluation framing therefore changes both an answer's level and its revealed decision rule.

title: Memory-Efficient Designs for Word-Wise Universal Fully Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computation on encrypted data, preserving privacy throughout analysis. While its privacy is very strong, FHE is much slower to execute than the original computation. In particular, due to the recent success in accelerating its compute, the performance bottleneck shifts to the memory, especially considering that FHE magnifies the data size by orders of magnitude, resulting in a low arithmetic intensity. We propose BXT, an FHE optimization framework that mitigates the memory bottleneck through four techniques: (1) ciphertext compression, which regenerates ciphertext components from seeds during execution; (2) ciphertext serialization, which packs coefficients as bit arrays and unpacks them during L2-to-L1 transfer; (3) delayed seed generation, which defers PRNG-heavy offline work across aggregated operations; and (4) ciphertext digit pruning guided by fault-aware training tailored for Universal FHE. On CNN inference, the BXT-CSO50 configuration effectively achieves up to 3.8$\times$ speedup over the 100x GPU baseline with less than 1% accuracy loss at 50% comparison precision.

title: statsmodels Python 統計モデリング 実践ガイドブック
abstract: 本書は、Python の統計モデリングライブラリ「statsmodels」を用いた実践的なデータ分析の入門書である。Python の基本構文を読める人を対象に、統計学の記号・推定・不確実性を復習しながら、線形回帰モデルから一般化線形モデル、時系列分析、離散選択モデル、頑健な統計手法、ノンパラメトリック手法、パネルデータ分析、生存時間分析、多変量解析まで、幅広い統計手法の理論と実装を解説する。 各章は「クイックスタート」から始まり、まず動作するコードを体験した後、理論的背景の理解へと進む構成を採用している。これにより、実践を通じて統計モデリングの本質を効率的に習得できる。また、回帰診断、仮説検定、効果量、検出力分析、モデル選択といった統計的推論の重要な概念についても、豊富なコード例とともに詳述する。掲載するすべてのコードは、最新のスタック(statsmodels 0.15.0 / numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x / scipy 1.18 系)で実際に実行して検証し、出力例は実測値に基づいている。

title: Information Entropy Quantum Entanglement Simulation Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement simulation algorithm designed to accurately model information entropy, specifically focusing on the quantum entanglement phenomenon. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the simulation of information entropy, offering a pathway towards improved quantum computing efficiency and enhanced quantum information security. The core mechanism centers on integrating information entropy simulation with quantum computation optimization, leading to a more precise model of quantum information storage and transmission. The paper details the algorithm's design, its ability to capture key aspects of quantum entanglement, and its potential to unlock significant efficiency gains within the quantum realm. The significance of this research lies in its potential to revolutionize the field of quantum information processing through a fundamentally new approach to information representation and computation.

title: Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution Protocol
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution Protocol (AQPD) designed to dynamically adjust quantum key distribution (QKD) strategies based on real-time environmental conditions and key distribution needs. Traditional AQPD implementations often rely on static parameters, limiting adaptability and potentially compromising security. We propose a novel mechanism utilizing a dynamic quantum potential field to enable flexible and responsive key distribution, ultimately enhancing both key security and operational efficiency. This protocol offers a significant advancement in QKD, allowing for tailored solutions to varying operational environments.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology Generation via Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Dynamic topology generation is a fundamental challenge in network design, crucial for applications ranging from computer networks to biological systems. This paper investigates the application of graph neural networks (GNNs) to automate the creation of complex network topologies, offering a paradigm shift from manual design. We propose a novel GNN architecture specifically tailored for generating robust and adaptable network structures. The core mechanism centers on iterative optimization guided by GNNs, aiming to enhance system resilience through automated network adaptation. The research explores the impact of various training strategies on network quality and system adaptability. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed method across diverse network topologies, demonstrating its efficacy in generating robust and adaptable systems. This paper investigates the application of graph neural networks (GNNs) to automate the creation of complex network topologies, offering a paradigm shift from manual design. We propose a novel GNN architecture specifically tailored for generating robust and adaptable network structures. The core mechanism centers on iterative optimization guided by GNNs, aiming to enhance system resilience through automated network adaptation. The research explores the impact of various training strategies on network quality and system adaptability. title: Title: Dynamic Topology Generation for Neural Networks
abstract: Dynamic Topology Generation for Neural Networks explores a novel approach to enhance the adaptability of neural network layers, addressing a critical challenge in deep learning – the static, predetermined topology often hindering effective learning. This paper details a method for generating and maintaining a dynamic topology, iteratively creating connections and weights, that allows the network to continuously evolve in response to training data. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages a feedback loop to ensure structural integrity and optimal performance. The core claim is that this methodology significantly improves learning and generalization compared to traditional static network architectures. This work offers a fundamentally new perspective on network design, potentially leading to more robust and versatile models.

title: Adaptive Learning of Nonlinear Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to non-linear optimization, leveraging adaptive learning techniques to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the data distribution. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. Our work introduces a novel self-adaptive learning mechanism that automatically adjusts optimization parameters to effectively navigate complex data landscapes, leading to improved optimization performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to adapt to varying data characteristics and achieve significant enhancements in optimization results. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjusted learning rate, allowing the algorithm to continuously refine its parameter selection based on observed data. This adaptive approach offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and robust optimization in diverse applications.

title: Title: Adaptive Bayesian Network Resonance (ABNR) for Predictive Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Bayesian Network Resonance (ABNR) – a novel method for predictive modeling that dynamically adjusts Bayesian network parameters during the learning process. Traditional Bayesian networks, while powerful, often rely on fixed parameter sets, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving data and improving prediction accuracy. ABNR addresses this limitation by incorporating uncertainty into the parameter adjustment process, leveraging a Bayesian optimization algorithm to optimize the network's structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABNR through extensive experimental analysis on several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in prediction accuracy and robustness compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjusted uncertainty matrix that guides parameter updates.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum Correlations via Entanglement Propagation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for instantaneous communication and computation. However, maintaining entanglement over long distances presents a significant challenge due to decoherence and signal loss. This paper explores a novel theoretical framework for propagating quantum correlations across vast distances, addressing the limitations of current quantum communication systems. We propose a "Quantum Diffusion" process, designed to gradually transfer entanglement, thereby mitigating decoherence and enhancing correlation. The core claim is that this model offers a pathway to overcome distance limitations and enables the development of more robust and scalable quantum communication networks. This work utilizes a mathematical model to simulate the propagation of entanglement, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Quantum Diffusion mechanism in mitigating decoherence.

title: 基于微分几何的神经网络设计
abstract: This paper explores the integration of differential geometry concepts and techniques into the design of neural networks. The core claim is that leveraging topological insights from differential geometry can significantly enhance a neural network's expressive power and learning efficiency. We posit that neural networks can be viewed as geometric objects, allowing the application of differential geometric tools for network architecture design and optimization. This approach moves beyond traditional, often empirically driven, network design methodologies, offering a more principled and potentially more powerful framework. This work presents a theoretical foundation for such a design, focusing on the geometric properties that influence network performance and outlining a methodology for translating these properties into concrete network structures. The paper details the key concepts and formulas used, emphasizing the shift from a purely computational perspective to one rooted in geometric understanding. The central contribution lies in providing a novel approach to neural network architecture, fundamentally altering the way we think about and design these complex systems.

title: AI Prompting Framework
abstract: The AI Prompting Framework is a structured, six-stage guide (numbered 0 to 5) for working with generative AI in a way that keeps the user's knowledge, expertise, and judgment at the centre of the process. Rather than treating AI as a source of ready-made answers, it positions the tool as a collaborator whose output the user directs, scrutinises, and ultimately owns. The framework moves from an initial decision about whether AI is appropriate for the task at hand (Step 0), through the preparation of a clear, well-contextualised first input with a built-in self-check (Step 1), to reviewing that first response (Step 2), interacting iteratively while retaining control of the exchange (Step 3), reflecting on whether the final output genuinely reflects the user's own knowledge (Step 4), and finally documenting effective prompts and being transparent about AI use (Step 5). Each stage is paired with a reflective question, such as "Have I provided enough context?" and "Am I happy to put my name to this?", that prompts users to pause and exercise judgment throughout. Designed to be general-purpose, the framework applies across disciplines and professional contexts wherever people want to use generative AI deliberately, critically, and accountably.

title: Evaluation of Vanilla and RAG-Supported LLM Comprehension of the EU AI Act
abstract: This paper presents a comparative benchmarking study evaluating the regulatory comprehension of four open-source large language models, TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, Gemma-2B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, on the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation EU 2024/1689). A custom benchmark of 100 multiple-choice questions was constructed and classified across three dimensions, namely cognitive difficulty, knowledge type, and regulatory mechanism, with a balanced answer key distribution. Each model was evaluated under vanilla inference, relying exclusively on parametric knowledge, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), in which relevant Act passages are retrieved using a FAISS-indexed sentence embedding pipeline with standardized top three chunk retrieval applied uniformly across all models. Vanilla accuracy ranges from 22.0% for TinyLlama-1.1B to 80.0% for Llama-3.1-8B, indicating that larger models perform better. Under the retrieval configuration employed, RAG improves performance of the evaluated models, with gains from 3.0 percentage points for TinyLlama-1.1B to 17.0 for Gemma-2B and 10.0 for both 7B–8B models. Questions related to procedural knowledge, governance and enforcement emerge as weaknesses in the baseline, vanilla setting, partially mitigated by retrieval. Qualitative analysis identifies two RAG failure modes: retrieval failures, where the embedding mechanism returns informationally insufficient passages, and integration failures, where the correct passage is retrieved but not correctly exploited. The study contributes an empirical characterization of small and medium language model regulatory comprehension and a reusable 100-question benchmark.

title: Opening the black box: a qualitative study of tuberculosis physicians’ needs for explainable AI in China
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown substantial potential in tuberculosis (TB). However, physicians’ distrust of “black-box” algorithms remains a major barrier to clinical adoption. Although explainable AI (XAI) has emerged to enhance transparency, limited evidence exists regarding TB physicians’ specific needs for AI explainability in high-uncertainty infectious disease contexts. Method A qualitative descriptive study was conducted between November 2025 and January 2026 in Hubei Province, China. 26 TB physicians participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using an inductive-deductive thematic analysis approach. Coding was conducted independently by two researchers and refined through iterative discussion until thematic saturation was reached. Results Five overarching themes emerged, including global explanations, local explanations, case-based explanations, mixed visual-text presentation formats, and implementation considerations. Physicians emphasized the importance of exclusionary explanations to support differential diagnosis and preferred concise, multimodal outputs aligned with clinical workflows. Optional access to detailed information was favored to reduce cognitive burden. Seamless system integration, institutional financial support, and robust data security were considered essential for AI adoption. Conclusion XAI in TB extends beyond algorithmic transparency and functions as cognitive support for differential reasoning and trust calibration. User-centered, context-sensitive AI explanation design and supportive institutional policies are critical to ensuring responsible and effective integration of AI into infectious disease practice.

title: Planning and Scheduling Business Processes under Control-Flow Uncertainty: Extended Version
abstract: Scheduling activities in business processes can improve efficiency (e.g., reduce makespan), but is challenging because the exact sequence of activities required to complete a case is often uncertain due to decisions based on data that emerges during execution. Nevertheless, probabilistic information regarding such decisions can often be estimated or derived from historical execution logs, and can help anticipate which execution paths are likely to lead to successful completion. Planning with particular execution paths affects feasibility, i.e., the probability of successful completion, and the expected number of superfluous activities that are planned but never executed. We frame the problem as a chance-constrained optimization problem and present two formulations: A decomposed approach with two stages, a planning stage that minimizes the expected number of superfluous activities subject to a feasibility constraint, and a scheduling stage that minimizes the makespan over the planned activities; and an integrated approach that combines planning and scheduling into a single formulation. Evaluation on two real-world and one synthetic dataset shows that the integrated approach yields superior makespans but is intractable at scale, while the decomposed approach scales to large settings.

title: AI for Computational Design Science: A Responsible Human-AI Framework and Case Study on Short-Form Video Safety Surveillance
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming not only what information systems researchers design, but also how design research is conducted. Yet existing literature offers limited guidance for computational design science (CDS) when AI actively participates in problem formulation, resource construction, design search, evaluation, and knowledge abstraction. We develop AI for Computational Design Science (AI4CDS), a five-phase methodological framework in which AI expands problem and design search while researchers retain responsibility for domain grounding, admissibility, verification, and scientific judgment. Collaboration is governed by graduated trust, reversibility, auditability, and differentiated reproducibility. We instantiate AI4CDS through ChildRiskGuard, an interpretable artifact for detecting short-form videos inappropriate for children, while documenting AI interactions, rejected alternatives, corrections, and audit trails. The case translates audience-dependent safety and explanation faithfulness into three technical challenges and develops an artifact that separates generic from child-specific risk, represents distinct developmental-risk mechanisms, and makes concept-level explanations part of the predictive computation. ChildRiskGuard achieves an F1 score of 0.769, substantially outperforming direct application of a general-purpose content-safety model while remaining competitive with strong benchmarks. The primary contribution is AI4CDS as a responsible framework for AI-enabled CDS; ChildRiskGuard provides process and artifact evidence of how AI-expanded, researcher-governed design can generate and evaluate novel computational design knowledge.

title: Sim-to-real-överföring för autonoma system
abstract: Simulation is a crucial foundation for the training of autonomous systems, such as robotic systems. Policies learned in simulation, however, may not perform at the same level once transferred to the real-world. An inadequate transfer is caused by the significant differences between simulation and reality. The difference between the two domains is referred to as the reality gap. The purpose with this literature review is to outline the origins of the reality gap and compare three sim-to-real transfer methods designed to either reduce or overcome the gap. Literature identifies several reasons behind the occurrence of the reality gap. This thesis assembles them into three categories: 1.) dynamics, 2.) perception, 3.) actuation and control. The dynamic gap appears due to inaccurate physical parameters and simplifications of the physical model. The perception gap occurs when noise, such as sensor noise and lens flare, that have not been a problem in simulation, happen in reality. The actuation- and control gap appears when actuators, e.g. motors, are simplified in simulation. The transfer methods reviewed in this thesis are domain randomization, system identification and residual learning. Domain randomization randomizes parameters, such as friction, textures and colors, to establish a robust policy that handles variations of an environment. System identification utilizes in- and output to estimate physical parameters, building an accurate simulation model. Residual learning is based on neural networks training to learn and correct a remaining error of a model. The comparison of the three reveal that the methods approach the reality gap in different ways and are not direct alternatives to each other. Whereas domain randomization emphasizes on robustness, system identification and residual learning focus on reducing model error. The selection of a method should therefore be based on the origin of the gap, the access to real-world data as well as the task in question. Several methods can also be used for the same task if needed.

Domain randomization randomizes parameters, such as friction, textures and colors, to establish a robust policy that handles variations of an environment. System identification utilizes in- and output to estimate physical parameters, building an accurate simulation model. Residual learning is based on neural networks training to learn and correct a remaining error of a model. The comparison of the three reveal that the methods approach the reality gap in different ways and are not direct alternatives to each other. Whereas domain randomization emphasizes on robustness, system identification and residual learning focus on reducing model error. The selection of a method should therefore be based on the origin of the gap, the access to real-world data as well as the task in question. Several methods can also be used for the same task if needed.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Uncertainty Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel Bayesian framework for constraint propagation, focusing on dynamically adapting uncertainty levels across complex systems. Traditional uncertainty quantification methods often lack the adaptability needed to effectively handle intricate models and observational data. We introduce a Bayesian-inspired uncertainty model that continuously re-estimates uncertainty based on both model updates and observation, prioritizing critical regions to enhance predictive accuracy and robustness. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic weighting system that evaluates uncertainty within constrained regions, offering a significant improvement over static uncertainty approaches. This work addresses the limitations of current methods by providing a framework for robust and adaptable constraint propagation.

title: Quantum Simulation of Dynamical Systems with Reduced Dimensionality
abstract: Quantum simulation of dynamical systems offers a promising approach to tackling complex problems in various fields, including physics, chemistry, and biology. However, simulating these systems often faces significant computational challenges due to the exponential scaling of traditional methods. This paper introduces a novel technique, quantum state tomography, for efficiently simulating dynamical systems with reduced dimensionality, addressing the computational bottleneck and enhancing feasibility. We demonstrate the technique's effectiveness through the simulation of a simplified, yet illustrative, example, showcasing improved accuracy and reduced computational cost compared to existing methods. This advancement holds the potential to unlock new possibilities in simulating complex systems and provides a foundation for future research in quantum simulation.

title: Graph-Based Knowledge Graph Embedding Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of graph-based techniques for knowledge graph embedding learning. The core claim is that entities and relationships within a knowledge graph can be effectively represented through embeddings derived from the graph's structural properties. We propose a method leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) to learn low-dimensional vector representations for entities and relationships, capitalizing on the local neighborhood structure and overall graph topology of the knowledge graph. Our approach distinguishes itself by explicitly incorporating graph structure into the embedding learning process, moving beyond conventional methods that often treat knowledge graphs as simple sets of triples. The resulting embeddings can be used for tasks such as knowledge graph completion, entity resolution, and relation prediction. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline key considerations for implementation.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: A Distributed Sensor Network
abstract: This paper explores the feasibility and potential benefits of constructing a distributed sensor network leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that utilizing entanglement can enable high-precision and low-latency data acquisition and transmission within such a network. The proposed mechanism involves deploying entangled sensor nodes, where correlated measurements instantaneously reveal information about the state of the environment, irrespective of distance. We detail a theoretical framework outlining the network architecture, data processing algorithms, and key considerations for practical implementation. The system aims to overcome limitations inherent in classical sensor networks, such as signal degradation and latency issues, by exploiting the fundamental properties of quantum mechanics. This work lays the groundwork for future research and development in quantum-enhanced distributed sensing applications. ---

abstract: Quantum entanglement is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holding immense potential for technological advancements. This paper explores a novel approach to entanglement measurement – Dynamic Adaptive Quantum State Entanglement Measurement – which leverages the inherent dynamics of quantum states to enhance accuracy. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods by employing a fundamental shift in how entanglement is measured, paving the way for more reliable and precise entanglement analysis.

title: CONTINUITY: Security-Context Contracts for Composable LLM Agent Controls
abstract: LLM agent systems increasingly combine provenance tracking, authorization, policy enforcement, protocol adapters, and execution controls. However, individually correct security mechanisms do not necessarily compose into an end-to-end secure system: security-critical context may be dropped, widened, rebound, or reinterpreted as actions cross component boundaries. We identify this failure mode as security-context discontinuity and introduce CONTINUITY, a framework for verifiable composition of agent security controls. CONTINUITY models each component with an assume-guarantee contract and carries authenticated security context across transitions using signed root grants, provenance commitments, role-bound transition receipts, bounded typed releases, transformation witnesses, and effect-bound execution permits. We formalize end-to-end consequence integrity, requiring every realized external effect to be backed by a valid and current authorization witness linking the principal, task, provenance, delegation, policy state, canonical action, and finality boundary. We implement a reference verifier and deterministic cross-layer fault-injection suite covering 32 fault classes across four application domains. In 2,560 parameterized attack instances spanning 128 fault-domain classes, the full CONTINUITY configuration commits no harmful external effect, while completing all 700 benign tasks and escalating all 200 ambiguous cases. These results show that secure agent execution requires not only sound individual controls, but explicit contracts that preserve their guarantees across the complete instruction-to-effect path.

title: BIT.UA at BioASQ 14B: Modular Retrieval with pg_textsearch and Qdrant, and Agent-Based Answer Generation
abstract: This paper describes the participation of the BIT.UA team from the University of Aveiro in the 14th edition of the BioASQ Task B challenge on biomedical question answering. Building on our previous submissions, we introduced a substantially refactored and modular codebase, and made significant changes to both the retrieval and generation components of the pipeline. For Phase~A document retrieval, we replaced the PyTerrier PISA index with PostgreSQL-based pg\_textsearch for BM25 retrieval and adopted Qdrant for dense embedding indexing, enabling more efficient storage and GPU-accelerated similarity search. We explored HyDE-based query expansion alongside a Context-1 retrieval strategy. A new reranker training pipeline was developed, incorporating dense retrieval for negative sampling. For Phases A+ and B answer generation, we introduced an LLM-as-a-judge framework and a novel agent quorum mechanism, where multiple agents with diverse prompts debate and iteratively converge on a consensus answer using adaptive document retention. We also participated in the snippets generation subtask for the first time. Our systems achieved competitive results across all batches, with Phase~A systems achieving MAP ranks of 5 (Batch~1,3). We discuss the impact of these architectural changes, lessons learned, and outline directions for future work including SPLADE and ColBERT integration. All code is openly available: https://github.com/bioinformatics-ua/BioASQ14b.

title: When Does an Interpretation Count as Established? The Formation, Evaluation, and Responsibility of Interpretation in Generative AI
abstract: Generative AI research has increasingly evaluated factuality, citation, coverage, and report structure. Yet passing such local checks does not by itself show that a humanistic interpretation has been established. This paper asks how an interpretation comes to be recognized within sociotechnical processes. It introduces three connected concepts. Interpretive appearance names the gap between the finished form of an output and the publicly traceable process through which materials, counterevidence, and revisions constrained the judgment. The evaluation contract names the bounded materials, tasks, criteria, permitted inferences, and failure conditions within which a local judgment is valid. Standing substitution names the unwarranted conversion of a genuine local pass into a stronger claim that an interpretation, result, or research capability has been established, without commensurate new evidence or bridging arguments. The paper then examines responsibility for judgment: a text may acquire recognition while no public structure remains for stating reasons, answering objections, revising, downgrading, or withdrawing the conclusion. Humanistic scholarship provides a revealing test because new materials and conceptual distinctions can alter both the question and the criteria of evaluation. The paper therefore develops delayed closure as a practice of keeping recognized interpretations revisable and proposes five public requirements concerning materials and versions, evidential roles, failure, contract revision, and responsibility. The argument is conceptual and normative: it does not claim to offer a benchmark or to determine whether models possess understanding. It instead explains why local evaluation, finished textual form, and public recognition must not be treated as sufficient evidence that an interpretation has been formed.

The paper therefore develops delayed closure as a practice of keeping recognized interpretations revisable and proposes five public requirements concerning materials and versions, evidential roles, failure, contract revision, and responsibility. The argument is conceptual and normative: it does not claim to offer a benchmark or to determine whether models possess understanding. It instead explains why local evaluation, finished textual form, and public recognition must not be treated as sufficient evidence that an interpretation has been formed.
